rules.comment: Per-user concurrent session limits require per-user identity; shared local-auth keys provide none. Enforce Entra ID-only auth and application-level enforcement.
Organization-level identity integration requires Entra ID-only auth; current key-based auth does not integrate account management automation.
Requests made with shared account keys cannot be attributed to individual users; non-repudiation requires Entra ID-only auth and audit trail.
Audit record timestamps are generated by the Cosmos DB platform infrastructure clocks and recorded in UTC.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
Cosmos DB is an Azure PaaS service; the software and configuration reside in Microsoft-managed platform infrastructure, entirely separate from any customer host OS.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
Cosmos DB does not expose the capability to execute external executables from the database service.

No password-based authentication to the DBMS is employed. Authentication uses either machine-generated account keys (not user-selected passwords) or Entra ID. If password-based authentication is later introduced, review with Entra ID policy.
No password-based authentication to the DBMS is employed; there are no user passwords for the DBMS to hash or store.
Authentication secrets are never transmitted in cleartext; endpoint access is restricted to TLS 1.2+ (minimalTlsVersion=Tls12) and key-based requests use HMAC signatures.
Azure Govcloud uses DoW-approved CAs.
Human review (PKI): the DBMS stores no customer PKI private keys; CMK (if adopted) resides in Azure Key Vault. Confirm organization requirements.
Azure Govcloud uses DoW-approved CAs.
Cosmos DB does not echo passwords or secret keys during authentication; secrets are managed only via the management plane.
Cosmos DB uses FIPS-validated platform cryptographic modules for transport and at-rest encryption.
Cosmos DB separates management-plane (portal/ARM) functionality from data-plane (SDK/SQL API) functionality.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
The Cosmos DB platform fails to a secure state on init/shutdown; Microsoft operates the platform for availability and integrity.
The Cosmos DB platform preserves fault telemetry and supports quick failover/recovery (enableAutomaticFailover=True on this account).
Cosmos DB security functions (authentication, authorization, encryption, auditing) are implemented in the platform layer, isolated from application data functions.
Human review: confirm data-transfer policy enforcement (network ACLs, restricted containers) meets requirements.
Cosmos DB accounts are isolated by the Azure platform; no shared customer-accessible system resources provide unintended information transfer between accounts.
Account keys allow anyone possessing the key direct data-plane access bypassing per-user authorization; disable local auth to enforce per-user access.
Application-layer input validation. Cosmos DB does not provide dynamic execution surfaces for the customer beyond documented stored procedures.
Application-layer input validation. Cosmos DB does not provide dynamic execution surfaces for the customer beyond documented stored procedures.
Application-layer input validation. Cosmos DB does not provide dynamic execution surfaces for the customer beyond documented stored procedures.
Application-layer rule: error message sanitization.
Detailed error access control requires per-user roles; shared local-auth keys cannot distinguish DBA from ordinary users. Enforce Entra ID-only auth.
Idle session termination and identity-aware disconnect require per-user sessions; shared local-auth keys make this unenforceable. Enforce Entra ID-only auth.
Logout/session termination requires per-user identity; shared local-auth keys make this unenforceable. Enforce Entra ID-only auth.
Security labels are not required for this system.
Security labels are not required for this system.
Security labels in transmission require per-user accountability; shared local-auth keys prevent enforcement. Enforce Entra ID-only auth.
Data-plane privileged operations cannot be restricted per user while shared account keys are enabled; Entra ID-only RBAC is required.
Elevated-privilege module execution cannot be restricted per user while shared account keys are enabled; no user-defined code with elevated privileges should be deployed.
Audit record timestamps are recorded in UTC by the Cosmos DB platform.
Timestamp granularity assurance comes from the centralized audit pipeline (Log Analytics records ISO 8601 millisecond timestamps).
Human review: confirm reauthentication circumstances (e.g., Entra ID session policies) meet organization requirements.
Account keys (cached authenticators) never expire and can be cached indefinitely by clients; no cache lifetime is enforceable. Use Entra ID tokens, which expire per policy, instead of keys.
Azure Govcloud uses DoW-approved CAs.
Cosmos DB processes execute in isolated platform-managed execution domains separating each account.
Human review (application layer): confirm invalid input handling is predictable and documented.
Azure Cosmos DB is fully managed; replaced components are removed by the platform during automatic updates.
Azure Cosmos DB is fully managed; Microsoft applies security updates to the underlying platform within its patching obligations.
Key-based requests are anonymous (no per-user identity); concurrent-logon detection is impossible until Entra ID-only auth is enforced. Entra ID sign-in logs can then provide this.
Cosmos DB uses FIPS-validated platform cryptographic modules for digital signature operations.
Cosmos DB uses FIPS-validated platform cryptographic modules for hashing operations.
Cosmos DB uses FIPS-validated platform cryptographic modules for confidentiality operations.
Inherited by the Cloud Service Provider.
Not a classified system.
Account keys cannot be associated with users or expired; user accounts expire via Entra ID lifecycle only when Entra ID-only auth is enforced.
Account keys are not associated with user identity; disabled users can retain valid keys. Enforce Entra ID-only auth so identity removal revokes access.
Cosmos DB is a fully managed PaaS; the customer cannot install software or firmware components on the DBMS platform.
Account keys are shared secrets not tied to individual users; individual authentication requires Entra ID-only auth (disableLocalAuth=true).
Key-based authentication provides no multifactor capability (a single secret grants full access); require Entra ID MFA for all privileged access.
Key-based authentication provides no multifactor capability (a single secret grants full access); require Entra ID MFA.

No password-based authentication is employed. Account keys are machine-generated 256-bit random secrets, not user-selected passwords; compromised secret rotation is available via key regeneration in the management plane.
No password-based authentication is employed; no commonly-used password list applies. Account keys are regenerated by the customer in the management plane as needed.
No password-based authentication is employed; suspected compromise of account keys is addressed by regenerating keys in the management plane, not by a password list.
No user-selected passwords exist; account keys are machine-generated random secrets not checked against password lists.
No password-based authentication is employed; no user account recovery process exists at the DBMS to require a new DBMS password.
No user-selected passwords exist; the DBMS imposes no password length/character restrictions.
No user-selected passwords exist; password-strength tooling applies to the identity provider (Entra ID), not the DBMS.

Cosmos DB platform clocks synchronize to Microsoft's authoritative time infrastructure; audit records carry synchronized UTC timestamps.
Cosmos DB platform clocks are synchronized against Microsoft's authoritative time source by the service.
